summary.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see’ and is the simplified form of 視. The older 視 is traditionally analyzed with 見 for the meaning of seeing and 示 as a sound element; an early graph was interpreted as an eye above a standing person.

formation.text: The present graph 视 is the simplified counterpart of 視. In the traditional graph, 見 contributes the seeing-related meaning and 示 supplies a sound cue. A separate early form was interpreted as an eye over a standing figure, so the later compound analysis does not describe that pictograph.

history.text: A paleographic interpretation distinguishes early forms of 視 and 見 by the figure beneath the eye: standing in the form read as 視 and seated in 見. Standing-figure forms are also identified in Western Zhou bronzes. Alongside the pictographic spelling, an early form using 見 and 氏 as a phonetic element is reported. The curated oracle-style image is a modern redraw of the proposed early graph, not an ancient artifact image. An earlier reading of the standing-figure form as 望 was considered and rejected.
The received traditional graph 視 is analyzed as 見 plus 示, with 見 semantic and 示 phonetic. The current 视 is identified as its simplified form.

uncertainties.text: The standing-figure reading is a scholarly interpretation, and individual archaic examples may remain disputed; no absolute date is given for a specific oracle-bone token. The simplified-form relationship is identified in the supplied character accounts, though a character-specific official standard record was not retrieved.

示 is explicitly analyzed as phonetic in the traditional graph. A same-system reconstruction comparison with 視 was reported, but the table could not be inspected; current matching Mandarin readings do not by themselves demonstrate the ancient sound relationship.

senses.period: Shang oracle-bone evidence; individual token date unresolved
senses.text: The cited paleographic analysis identifies Shang oracle-bone contexts, including 視師 and 視方, as uses involving observing. The date of any individual token is not specified.

The traditional graph is glossed as looking toward, and later dictionary examples include examining or observing. When this use developed in relation to the basic looking or seeing sense is unresolved.
Current definitions include looking at, observing and seeing.

developments.text: Both uses are documented, but their chronological or derivational relationship is not established.

limitations.text: Other dictionary-attested uses include treating someone as, eyesight, caring for, administering, comparing, imitating, and a use glossed as 通「示」. Their chronology and connections are not established here.

overview.text: 视 means ‘look at’ or ‘see’ and is the simplified form of 視. The traditional graph combines 見, associated with seeing, and 示 as a sound element; an early graph was interpreted as an eye above a standing person.

relationships.text: The character accounts identify 视 as the simplified form of 視.
